card.title: Love Means Checking
card.instruction: Treat close monitoring of choices, moods, and details as care, becoming more involved whenever you feel uncertain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Text when you and Ben reach the cinema, love, so I know you're safe.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mum, my phone stays off during the film.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When does it finish? I'll wait up for your message.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're walking to dinner afterwards. We haven't chosen anywhere.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll drive behind you while you choose. You can keep your phone off; I'll see for myself that you're having a nice time.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 frames arrival reporting as safety, A3 waits for the next update, and A5 increases to physical surveillance when dinner plans become uncertain.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's phone-off boundary causes A3's finish-time question; B4's unchosen walking destination causes A5's follow-by-car plan.

relationship.evidence: B2 explains cinema etiquette and B4 supplies a normal undecided dinner plan.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's uncertainty to replace unavailable messages with direct observation, still calling it care.

specificity.evidence: A1-B2 establish a mother checking a cinema trip with Ben; B4 changes the after-film plan.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's phone-can-stay-off concession earns its irony from replacing reporting with more intrusive monitoring.
